name: Shadow Puppetry
visualIdentity: The source explicitly describes readable silhouettes on a translucent screen, separated into depth layers. Keep props legible in outline, limbs distinct from torsos, and shadow direction and size consistent with one light source. The palette suggestion is warm screen and dark ink.
suitableUses: Explicitly suitable for folk tales, theatrical moments, fables, cultural storytelling, and landscape scenes. Its chaptered storytelling patterns may suit explanatory or editorial narratives, product introductions, or cinematic sequences when they have meaningful progression. These broader uses are inferred; choose a chapter structure only when it serves the subject.
limitations: Avoid crowded or ambiguous outlines, exposed puppet joints, rubbery stretching, colored rig parts, and any lighting that breaks the single-source logic. Omit chapter transitions when the topic is too short, they obscure causality, or a cut conflicts with a continuous-shot or loop requirement. Use no transition pattern when no candidate fits.
palette: For new artwork without an approved palette, the suggestion is background #EFE0BC and foreground #272821, exactly two base colors, with no gradient or added accent hues. These are suggestions, not canonical values. Preserve task, brand, reference, semantic-role, and asset colors exactly; use opacity, hatching, or screen patterns for tonal variation. Check contrast on composited frames; the listed 11.375 ratio applies only to opaque sRGB tokens.
motionAndInteraction: Animate puppet poses, shadow size, and stage movement with defined pivots, separated limbs, and coherent light. Do not impose stop-motion stepping from the name alone. Optional chapter handoffs or story steps can coordinate copy and scenes; for video, schedule them on seekable composition time with reading holds. For interactive HTML, finite scroll progress can scrub states and transitions; backward and direct seeks must restore coherent states. Respect keyboard, touch, and reduced-motion needs where applicable.
audio: No fixed genre, tempo, instrument, voice, or required layer is specified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied assets and explicit requirements. Synchronize through the render pipeline, then check speech clarity, balance, clipping, and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Prepare layered silhouettes, a translucent screen, legible props, and puppet pivots; separate screen and puppet layers so they can move independently. Supply authorized fonts, artwork, and audio as needed. Cache or deterministically replay stateful motion, seed randomness, and distinguish simulated appearance from photographed production.
combinations: Use alone for theatrical moments. Style-091 rigging is suggested for believable articulated silhouettes with pivots and joint limits, while preserving solid ink and separated limbs. Style-038 can add static, low-opacity foreground-ink washes behind puppets without new hues. These are optional hybrids; maintain contrast and avoid loose mixing of ink traditions.
productionApproach: SVG and Canvas 2D are the recommended visual tools; GSAP is the primary motion engine for deterministic, seekable timelines. Motion is optional if seeking is explicitly synchronized and verified. HyperFrames owns scene assembly, timing, media and audio sync, validation, and export; Remotion is only a documented fallback when HyperFrames is unavailable or verified unable to meet a requirement. Keep visual construction and motion logic in their own layers, select tools by fidelity and medium, and inspect key frames and the full video.
